title: Pro-etale locality and pullback of dualizable condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, and $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of dualizable objects (objects admitting evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities). For a profinite set $S$, use the analogous notation for sheaves on profinite sets over $S$, with finite jointly surjective covering families and coefficient ring the restriction of $\Lambda$ to that site. For every morphism of schemes $f:T\to X$, the coefficient identification $f^*\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_T$ makes inverse image an exact symmetric monoidal functor $f^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(T,\Lambda)$. It preserves dualizable objects and commutes with the scalar extensions $\Lambda_X\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$, where $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ and $P\in D(R)$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Moreover, for every pro-etale covering family $\{U_i\to X\}$ and every $K\in D(X,\Lambda)$,
$$K\text{ is dualizable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K|_{U_i}\text{ is dualizable for every }i.$$
There is no quasi-compactness or bound on irreducible components of $X$ or $U_i$ in this assertion.

source.place: Section 3, pullback paragraph before (3.1); Definition 3.3 and Lemma 4.5, lisse assertion

proof.text: For a scheme morphism $f:T\to X$, [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] gives the ring isomorphism $\alpha_f:f^*\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_T$ (both rings commutative since $\Lambda$ is). With $c=\alpha_f$, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] supplies the exact module inverse image $f^*$ and its unbounded derived functor $Lf^*$, computed termwise, which is triangulated, hence exact. The derived tensor comparison $Lf^*(F\otimes^L G)\cong Lf^*F\otimes^LLf^*G$ is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] this comparison and the unit comparison $Lf^*\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_T$ commute with associators, unitors and symmetries, so $Lf^*$ is strong symmetric monoidal for the closed symmetric monoidal structures of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Scalar extension: by [def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization], $\Lambda_X\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$ (constant-section structure map, constant realization of [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]) is $D(p_X^*)(N_P)$, where $N_P=D(e^{-1})Lc^*\underline P\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$ is formed on the point and does not depend on $X$; likewise for $T$ with the same $N_P$. For a $\Lambda$-module sheaf $M$ on $*_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the natural isomorphism $\varphi_M:f^*p_X^*M\cong p_T^*M$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] is monoidal and its component at $\Lambda$ is $\alpha_f$ by definition of $\alpha_f$. Applying naturality and monoidality to the action $\Lambda\otimes M\to M$ shows that $\varphi_M$ carries the $f^{-1}\Lambda_X$-action on $f^{-1}p_X^*M$, transported along $\alpha_f$, to the $\Lambda_T$-action on $p_T^*M$. By the final paragraph of the module construction in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $f^*(p_X^*M)=f^{-1}p_X^*M\otimes_{f^{-1}\Lambda_X,\alpha_f}\Lambda_T$ is $f^{-1}p_X^*M$ with exactly this transported action, so $\varphi$ is a natural isomorphism $f^*\circ p_X^*\cong p_T^*$ of functors $\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_T)$. All functors involved are exact and act termwise on complexes, so $\varphi$ induces a natural isomorphism $Lf^*\circ D(p_X^*)\cong D(p_T^*)$, and evaluating it at $N_P$ gives $Lf^*(\Lambda_X\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P)\cong\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$, natural in $P$.

A strong symmetric monoidal functor sends the evaluation and coevaluation maps of a dualizable object to evaluation and coevaluation maps for its image; functoriality of the tensor comparison transports both triangle identities. Hence every scheme inverse image $f^*$ preserves dualizable objects.

source.place: Definition 3.3 and the monoidal pullback assertion in Section 3

proof.text: Let $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}$ be a pro-etale covering family. By [lem-zl-condensed-cover-restriction-conservative] the derived inverse images $Lu_i^*$, formed with $\alpha_{u_i}$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], are jointly conservative. They are the restrictions $K\mapsto K|_{U_i}$ of the statement: clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the localized site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_i$, and clause 1 of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], which holds for every sheaf of sets, abelian groups or rings with no constancy hypothesis, gives $u_i^{-1}G\cong G|_{U_i}$ naturally in $G$. In particular $u_i^{-1}\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_X|_{U_i}$ as rings, and composing with $\alpha_{u_i}$ gives $\Lambda_X|_{U_i}\cong\Lambda_{U_i}$. By the scalar-transport clause of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $u_i^*G$ is $u_i^{-1}G\cong G|_{U_i}$ with its action transported along this ring isomorphism. Since $u_i^*$ is exact and $Lu_i^*$ is termwise, $Lu_i^*K=K|_{U_i}$. The constant-ring clauses ((2) of the localization lemma, 2--3 of the restriction lemma) are not used, since $\Lambda_X$ need not be a constant sheaf.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, conservativity of restriction to a covering

proof.text: Under the identification of Step 3, each $u_i^*$ is the exact derived slice restriction $r$ for $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$, $U=U_i$. It is strong symmetric monoidal by Step 1, with tensorator the comparison $\rho$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for the localization morphism. The source and target categories carry the closed symmetric monoidal structures, internal Homs $R\mathcal Hom$ and natural tensor--Hom bijections $\operatorname{tr}$ of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. The natural isomorphism $h_i=\eta_{L,M}:r\,R\mathcal Hom(L,M)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{U_i}(rL,rM)$ is the slice comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The second displayed identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose], $\operatorname{tr}_U(r(f)\circ\rho^{-1})=\eta\circ r(\operatorname{tr}(f))$, is exactly the transpose-preservation hypothesis of [lem-zl-dualizable-jointly-conservative-locality], and its third identity is the symmetry compatibility of the tensorator. With the joint conservativity of Step 3, all hypotheses of [lem-zl-dualizable-jointly-conservative-locality] hold for the family $(u_i^*)_{i\in I}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 proof, monoidality, conservativity, and internal Hom

proof.text: Applying [lem-zl-dualizable-jointly-conservative-locality] to $K$ and the restrictions $u_i^*$ gives $K$ dualizable if and only if every $K|_{U_i}$ is dualizable. No quasi-compactness or irreducible-component bound is used.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 and its stated locality conclusion

lean.statement: theorem condensed_dualizable_iff_proetale_cover (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X] (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : Scheme.Cover.{v} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X) (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X X))) : Nonempty (HasRightDual K) ↔ ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, Nonempty (HasRightDual ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ.X (𝒰.f i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))
